ranking.reasons: Only variant that actually delivers a tight behind-three-quarter MEDIUM shot per the prompt — the seam split fills a much larger share of the frame, profile face-turn reads clean, and CREAK-RIIIP SFX sells the beat.

Clean and verified — the flagged MISC-00 background shelving is just boxes/bottles, no extra figures — but the crop is a wide near-full-body shot rather than the requested medium, so the seam payoff is small in frame.
Same wide near-full-body framing problem as r1v2 with a slightly less dynamic bubble placement, so it ranks just behind on composition tightness.
The only true CLOSE-UP of the four — face fills the frame with the sideways glance and temple sweat bead clearly readable, exactly matching the prompt's shot-scale request.
Tighter than v1/v2 and close to a CU, with good depth from the folding chair in the background, but still slightly wider than v4's true close crop.
Medium-close framing undercuts the requested CLOSE-UP, and the 'PROJECT VITALITY' signage competes for attention in the background.
Widest of the four and least CLOSE-UP-adherent, with an oversized bubble dominating the headroom instead of the requested tight face crop.

Closest to the requested torso-up diagonal: cropped at the thigh (not full body), Margo staged off-center to the right against the angled screen/wall lines for real FG/BG depth rather than a centered symmetrical composition.
Similar cowboy-length crop avoids full body, but Margo is centered with chairs symmetrically flanking her, undercutting the 'not centered-symmetrical' instruction.
Full body from feet up violates the torso-up requirement outright, though the doorway framing and 'I'm ready' line add some off-center depth.
Full body like v3 but worse — two disconnected empty speech bubbles floating top and bottom is a baked-lettering glitch on top of the shot-scale violation.
Cleanest true medium-close-up — head and shoulders centered, no macro over-crop, no necklace prop, and the eyes-widening panic reads clearly without competing detail.
Correct MCU crop and strong panic expression but the visible gold chain/necklace is an uncalled prop (PROP-01) that shouldn't be there.
Crops in tighter and more asymmetric than the requested head-and-shoulders framing, and carries the same PROP-01 necklace defect as v1.
Pulls back into more of a torso/medium shot rather than the requested MCU, diluting the panic close-up, and still shows the PROP-01 pendant.

Shoots past the squat-rack upright for real foreground-occlusion depth on a genuine low three-quarter angle, giving the panel the diagonal/FG-BG staging the flatter variants lack, with one coherent intact bar and a controlled-exhale expression.

Best directional key light and a legible power-rack background give real depth, but the lab coat is missing versus the character's established wardrobe, a continuity risk the owner has flagged before.
Reads correctly (intact single bar, coat present) but the lined-up folding chairs and flat diffuse lighting make the staging static compared to the other two.
Strongest raking key light modeling the shoulder plus a legible blurred-gym background for depth, and the tear reads unambiguously as frayed cloth threads over smooth intact skin.
Essentially the same strong lit composition and clean cloth-not-skin tear as v2, ranked just behind on marginally softer thread detail at the rip edge.
Keeps the gym location legible in the background and the tear renders as clean fabric over intact skin, but the lighting is flatter and the framing more static than v2/v3.
Loses the gym environment entirely for a plain studio-gray backdrop, breaking location continuity, and introduces an unestablished stone pendant not seen in the other variants.

True over-Margo's-shoulder torso-up two-shot with real depth staging (Kress large and sharp in the mid-ground, Margo's shoulder/hair anchoring the foreground) — the only variant that actually delivers the requested tight OTS composition.
Genuine depth-staged diagonal with Margo's back in FG and Kress readable behind her, but the frame pulls too wide to read as tight torso-up and shows more desk/environment than the beat calls for.
Torso-up crop is on-spec but the two figures are staged as a level, same-scale, face-to-face lineup — exactly the flat two-shot the staging guide forbids.
Full-body wide shot that directly violates the 'not full body' instruction and trips the dialogue-beat full-body-monotony penalty.

Best delivers 'the clipboard exchange dominating the frame' — the board fills the center of a tight torso-up OTS composition from behind Margo, with a strong diagonal reach that reads as dynamic theft rather than a static handoff.
Correctly stages the camera behind Margo's shoulder toward Kress with a slightly low angle, keeping the clipboard central, though it's a bit more static than v2's diagonal grab.
Clean tight medium-close two-shot with both faces readable and the clipboard prominent, but the camera is behind Kress's shoulder toward Margo — the reverse of the requested angle.
Full-body wide shot that violates the explicit 'not full body' instruction, shrinking the clipboard exchange to a small fraction of a busy frame.

Tightest true medium-shot crop of the three, keeping the flexed bicep and glowing amulet large and central while her gaze stays angled down and away from camera — no fourth-wall break, best payoff density.

Solid three-quarter medium shot with correct averted gaze and a well-lit amulet, but the flexed arm crosses tighter over the body so the bicep itself reads slightly smaller and more obscured than in v2.
Gaze and profile angle are correct, but the frame pulls down to the hips/thighs, drifting from 'medium shot' toward a wider full-body crop that dilutes the bicep/amulet payoff.

Body fully oversold: colossal round biceps, extreme curve overshoot past the ref sheet baseline; cast staged in genuine depth layers (cropped FG figure, mid-ground clappers, background figure at smaller scale); skylight backlight gives real rim glow on the low hero angle; face reads triumphant joy.

Lab coat and leggings smother the size/curve payoff (the exact 'generic' failure this beat must overshoot); cast arranged near-same depth in a left-to-right row (flat-lineup violation); arms-crossed pose reads flat.

b23-finale.one_liner: r4v2 bares the physique for a genuine overshoot of the ref's size ceiling and stages the cast in real depth layers, while r4v5's lab coat smothers the payoff and lines the cast up flat.
b23-finale.judge: fresh Sonnet subagent 2026-08-10, rubrics: qa-checklist.md + cinematic-framing.md + owner-defect-feedback-2026-08-10.md

ranking.reasons: Best-bent barbell sells 'impossibly loaded'; warm hard rim light cuts Margo off the dark background with long directional shadows; extreme low-angle diagonal; genuine three-depth staggering (investor FG bokeh, mid-sharp, soft background); peak gritted-teeth/vein/sweat face.
Strong low-angle diagonal, correct gray-tank wardrobe, clean three-layer depth; barbell bend and lighting a notch less dramatic.
Good bend and FG bokeh, real strain; Margo's top deviates from the ref tank (wardrobe ding).
Extreme low angle, strong grimace; barbell nearly straight; ambiguous symmetric FG arm occlusion.
Decent diagonal; FG investor too sharp for bokeh depth; barbell barely bends.
Lab-coat wardrobe break, straight bar, background closer to a lineup.

b18-money-lift.one_liner: r5v6 is the only variant where the barbell visibly bows under load, the rim light and shadows read genuinely directional rather than flat, and Margo's strained face carries real peak-effort intensity.
